seo_title: Hook Island Sea Monster: Le Serrec's 1964 photo, explained
seo_desc: Robert Le Serrec's 1964 photo of a giant tadpole on the sea floor off Hook Island, Queensland. What he said he saw, why it's called a hoax and what it probably was.
summary: A French photographer's 1964 shot of a giant tadpole lying on the sea floor off Queensland, and almost certainly a hoax.
body: The Hook Island sea monster is basically one set of photos. On 12 December 1964 a French photographer named Robert Le Serrec was crossing Stonehaven Bay at Hook Island in the Whitsundays with his family and a friend when, by their account, they spotted a huge dark tadpole-shaped animal lying on the bottom of the shallow lagoon. He took pictures, and by the time the story got around its length had grown to 75 or 80 ft (roughly 23 to 24 metres). I think it's a hoax, and so does pretty much everyone who has looked into it (the reasons are below).
The photos were published in Australia's Everyone magazine and went around the world. The best-known picture shows a broad head and a long, tapering tail under the water.

The case is widely considered a hoax. It came out that Le Serrec was in debt in France and had talked about making money from a sea-serpent photo before the trip. Suggested explanations range from a sheet or tarpaulin weighted on the sea bed to a large fish.
